business_model.claim: Products are sold in more than 85 countries through two channels, wholesale and direct-to-consumer. In 2025 the DTC share of consolidated revenues was 52.1%, up from 49.7% in 2024, and the wholesale share was 47.9%.

growth_thesis.claim: Management expects growth to continue, having raised the full-year 2026 revenue outlook to about 3% and adjusted diluted EPS to $14.45 to $14.65. For the outlook to be met, Q4 trends in both brands and the cost and tariff conditions above must hold.
quotes: Adjusted diluted earnings per share to be in the range of $14.45 to $14.65, up from our previous guidance range of $13.70 to $14.00.

material_events.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A (P3) and risk factors (P2)
material_events.claim: Crocs recorded non-cash impairments in 2025 on the HEYDUDE trademark ($430.0 million) and HEYDUDE reporting unit goodwill ($307.0 million), part of total asset impairments of $738.1 million. The triggering event came from lower HEYDUDE forecasts in the second quarter of 2025.
quotes: Asset impairments were $738.1 million, primarily driven by the partial impairment of the HEYDUDE indefinite-lived trademark and HEYDUDE Brand reporting unit goodwill.

material_events.claim: The Board increased the share repurchase authorization by $1.5 billion, leaving approximately $2.0 billion available for repurchase.
quotes: On July 30, 2026, the Company also announced that its Board of Directors (the “Board”) authorized the increase of the Company’s existing common stock repurchase authorization by $1.5 billion.

material_events.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A (P4); the earnings release (P6) shows the adjustment
material_events.claim: Following the Supreme Court's IEEPA tariff ruling and the Court of International Trade's refund order, Crocs had received about $67 million of IEEPA tariff refunds, including interest. About $64 million was booked as a benefit in cost of sales in the third quarter. Management calls the refunds non-recurring.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, we received approximately $67 million of IEEPA tariff refunds, including interest.

material_events.basis: stated in the Q3 2026 earnings release (P6)
material_events.claim: Crocs raised its full-year 2026 outlook on October 29, 2026. It now expects revenues up approximately 3% and adjusted diluted EPS of $14.45 to $14.65, up from $13.70 to $14.00 previously.
quotes: Adjusted diluted earnings per share to be in the range of $14.45 to $14.65, up from our previous guidance range of $13.70 to $14.00.

risks.basis: stated in P4 and P6 (refund share of margin and non-recurring label); the effect on later periods is inferred.
risks.claim: Q3 2026 reported gross margin of 66.2% is lifted by IEEPA tariff refunds worth 630 basis points that the company calls non-recurring; adjusted gross margin was 60.3%, so the reported margin may overstate the run-rate.
quotes: These refunds are non-recurring.
Adjusted gross margin increased 180 basis points to 60.3% compared to 58.5%.

risks.basis: stated in P4; the cost impact on future periods is inferred.
risks.claim: Tariffs still in effect keep raising product costs, and the timing of the remaining IEEPA refunds is uncertain: about $67 million has been received against an estimated $75 million to $80 million eligible.
quotes: The tariffs that remain in effect continue to increase our product costs.
While the timing remains uncertain, we currently estimate that we are eligible to receive a total of approximately $75 million to $80 million in refunds related to these tariffs, including interest.

risks.basis: stated in P2, P3 and P4 for the history and the growth figures; the risk of further impairment is inferred, since the HEYDUDE share of the remaining balances is not given.
risks.claim: HEYDUDE recovery may not hold. Revenue grew 6.1% in Q3 but is still down (4.3)% for nine months. The prior-year impairments of $430.0 million (trademark) and $307.0 million (goodwill) show how a weak forecast can trigger large write-downs.
quotes: In the past, several footwear companies, including ours, have experienced periods of rapid growth in revenues and earnings followed by periods of declining revenues and losses, and our business may be similarly affected in the future.

risks.basis: figures stated in F1, F3, P4 and P7; the funding-pressure mechanism is inferred.
risks.claim: Buybacks are large relative to cash generation: repurchases of 506,194 (table in thousands) in nine months against operating cash flow of 561,189 (table in thousands), with long-term borrowings up to 1,289,044 (table in thousands) from 1,230,885 (table in thousands). A larger authorization adds scope for further debt-funded returns.
quotes: Additional future financing may be necessary to fund our operations and there can be no assurance that, if needed, we will be able to secure additional debt or equity financing on terms acceptable to us or at all.

risks.basis: stated in P4 (wholesale figures and cautionary language); the impact on later periods is inferred.
risks.claim: Demand risk in wholesale and in some distributor markets: Crocs Brand wholesale revenue fell (4.3)% over nine months, wholesale partners are described as acting cautiously, and Middle East conflict is cutting revenue in several distributor markets.
quotes: Given this, our wholesale partners are also acting cautiously.

risks.basis: balances stated in F1 and tax-rate volatility stated in P3; the possibility of an adverse outcome is inferred.
risks.claim: Tax balances are large and uncertain: deferred tax assets of 904,841 (table in thousands) and long-term income taxes payable of 641,563 (table in thousands) are tied to intellectual-property transactions, and the effective tax rate has been volatile.
quotes: Our effective tax rate has varied dramatically in recent years due to intra-entity intellectual property rights transactions, differences in our profitability levels and relative operating earnings across multiple jurisdictions, and by changes in the valuation allowance.

unresolved_questions.basis: Stated in P4 (estimate, amount received, non-recurring). The link to the reported versus adjusted gross margin gap is read from P6's reconciliation.
unresolved_questions.claim: How much of the remaining IEEPA tariff refund will arrive, and when? The filings say about $67 million of an estimated $75 million to $80 million has been received, and call the refunds non-recurring.
quotes: While the timing remains uncertain, we currently estimate that we are eligible to receive a total of approximately $75 million to $80 million in refunds related to these tariffs, including interest.

unresolved_questions.basis: Stated in P4 and P3. The question about the forward run-rate is inferred.
unresolved_questions.claim: What is the underlying gross margin once refunds are excluded, given tariffs that remain in effect? The 10-Q says duties are lower but still raise product costs, and further trade actions are unclear.
quotes: The tariffs that remain in effect continue to increase our product costs.

unresolved_questions.basis: Stated in P4 and P6 (figures and guidance). The sustainability question is inferred.
unresolved_questions.claim: Is HEYDUDE's return to growth durable? Q3 revenue rose, led by wholesale, but nine-month revenue is still down and full-year guidance is only about flat.
quotes: HEYDUDE Brand revenues increased 6.1%, or 6.2% on a constant currency basis, compared to the same period in 2025.

unresolved_questions.basis: Figures and the partner-caution statement are stated in P4. Persistence is inferred.
unresolved_questions.claim: Will Crocs Brand wholesale stay soft while direct-to-consumer carries growth? Crocs wholesale is down for nine months, and the filing says wholesale partners are acting cautiously.
quotes: Given this, our wholesale partners are also acting cautiously.

unresolved_questions.basis: Balances and cash flows are stated in F1 and F3. The tension with the debt-paydown statement is inferred.
unresolved_questions.claim: How are the buybacks being financed, and does debt paydown match the rhetoric? Long-term borrowings rose from year-end while repurchases ran well ahead of the prior year, and the authorization was expanded.
quotes: During the quarter, we returned $250 million to shareholders through share repurchases while continuing to strengthen our balance sheet through debt paydown.

unresolved_questions.basis: Balances are stated in F1 and the IP transaction context in P3. The resolution risk is inferred, and the underlying tax note was not in the packet.
unresolved_questions.claim: How will the uncertain tax positions on the intellectual property transactions resolve, and what is their effect on cash taxes and deferred tax assets? Long-term income taxes payable and deferred tax assets are both large against total equity.
quotes: The other relevant uncertain tax positions associated with the 2023 IP transactions remain unchanged.

unresolved_questions.basis: The effect is stated in P4 without any size. The question of how large it is is inferred.
unresolved_questions.claim: How large is the Middle East conflict's effect on distributor-market revenue and on raw material and transport costs? The 10-Q describes the effect only qualitatively.
quotes: Most recently, the conflict in the Middle East has caused, and may continue to cause, a reduction in our revenues for several of our distributor markets and an increase in the costs of raw materials and transportation associated with elevated oil prices.

verdict_reason: expected return -0.9 points a year against the required return over 3 years
